battle.name: 第一次馬其頓戰爭
battle.theater: 色雷斯海岸與愛琴海北岸
battle.brief: 西元前215至205年，第一次馬其頓戰爭在色雷斯海岸、馬其頓北部邊境與愛琴海北岸展開。迦太基海軍在梅托涅與埃維亞得手，馬其頓王國靠混合方陣頂住埃托利亞聯盟的游擊，最後靠羅馬促成的和約收場。卡面的斯巴達長矛正站在這一戰的起點：它仍是希臘盟軍重裝步兵的制式兵器，馬其頓方陣的薩里沙長矛已把它擠到側翼。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 第一次馬其頓戰爭是西元前215至205年間的一場戰爭，交戰主軸在馬其頓王國與希臘聯盟內部的反對者之間，迦太基則以海軍與錢糧從旁支撐。馬其頓一方以國王安托古斯三世·多松為核心，他在世時是科林斯同盟的盟主，麾下的編制是馬其頓方陣兵、希臘盟軍重裝步兵、阿格里亞諾斯標槍手、弓箭手與騎兵混在一起的混合大軍，腓力五世即位後沿用這套編制，並把戰線推入伯羅奔尼撒。希臘一方以埃托利亞聯盟為主，該聯盟拒絕接受馬其頓主導的同盟秩序，兵以標槍手與輕裝步兵為主，講求游擊、擾亂糧道與圍逼要地；阿卡亞聯盟由西庫昂的阿拉圖斯領導，名義上與馬其頓結盟，實則對腓力五世的擴張頗多戒心，戰事中一度與埃托利亞人併肩作戰。迦太基一方由西西里的海軍統帥漢諾與漢尼拔率艦隊進入愛琴海，先取埃維亞，再奪梅托涅，企圖把馬其頓的兵力和注意力釘在希臘本土，替義大利的戰局爭取喘息。羅馬沒有直接參戰，卻在西元前211年與埃托利亞人議和，又在西元前205年派出使節促成停戰，是這場戰爭背後最有力的一隻手。伊利里亞海盜、羅得島與帕加馬亦各自動向，後兩者站在馬其頓一方。
countriesEn: The First Macedonian War was fought between roughly 215 and 205 BC across the eastern Mediterranean, with the main line of conflict running between the kingdom of Macedon and the opponents of the Hellenic League inside Greece, while Carthage supported one side from the sea and with money and grain. On the Macedonian side the figure at the centre was King Antigonus III Doson, who as hegemon of the League of Corinth fought with a mixed army built out of Macedonian phalangites, Greek allied hoplites, Agrianian javelinmen, archers and cavalry; when Philip V came to the throne he kept that establishment and pushed the war into the Peloponnese. On the Greek side the principal opponent was the Aetolian League, which would not accept the Macedonian-led order of the Hellenic League and whose strength lay in javelinmen and light infantry given to harassment, to cutting supply lines and to the investing of towns; the Achaean League, led by Aratus of Sicyon, was formally allied with Macedon but watched the expansion of Philip V with real suspicion, and at one point fought alongside the Aetolians. On the Carthaginian side the commanders from Sicily, Hanno and Hannibal, both sons of Gisgo, carried a fleet into the Aegean, took Euboea and then Methone, and sought to pin Macedon's troops and attention in Greece so that the war in Italy could breathe. Rome did not fight in this war directly, but it made a separate peace with the Aetolians in 211 BC and then sent an embassy that brokered the end of the war in 205 BC, making it the strongest hand behind the conflict. Illyrian pirates, Rhodes and Pergamon each moved according to their own interest, the last two on the Macedonian side.
people: 這場戰爭裡真正推動局勢的人不多，但每一位都留下了可以追蹤的痕跡。安托古斯三世·多松是起點：他在科林斯同盟盟主的名位上平息同盟戰爭，於西元前222年的底拉修斯之戰擊敗斯巴達王克里奧美尼三世，迫使對方退位；轉年又圍攻埃托利亞人的守護地泰爾蒙，因後方消息而撤圍，這次失敗正是本戰爭的直接前因。他於西元前221年去世，留下九歲的腓力五世。腓力五世初由母后阿帕瑪與阿拉圖斯攝政，兩人很快決裂：阿拉圖斯軟禁了王宮內的反對者，又因埃托利亞問題與馬其頓各行其是；年少的國王此後親領兵馬，兩度進入伯羅奔尼撒，圍困麥加羅波利斯，終於把馬其頓的軍隊常駐在伯羅奔尼撒島上。阿拉圖斯是聯盟真正的靈魂，卻多病、缺乏兵權，只能靠聯盟機制維持局面。迦太基方面，漢諾與漢尼拔在梅托涅的一夜奇襲得手，接著漢諾在埃維亞沿岸與安托古斯周旋，最終在塞薩利基灣的海戰中敗退；帕加馬的歐洛克斯與羅得島的使節則在外交上替馬其頓拉攏援軍。停戰之後，攝政安托古斯曾策劃暗殺歸國的腓力五世，這一段被編年家波里比烏斯記了下來。
peopleEn: Few individuals drove the course of this war, but each of them left a trace that can be followed. Antigonus III Doson is the starting point: as hegemon of the League of Corinth he ended the War of the Allies and in 222 BC defeated the Spartan king Cleomenes III at Sellasia, forcing him to abdicate; the following year he besieged the Aetolian sanctuary at Thermon and had to lift the siege on news from his rear, and that failure is the direct antecedent of this war. He died in 221 BC and left the nine-year-old Philip V on the throne. The young king was at first governed by his mother Apama and by Aratus, and the two fell out quickly: Aratus removed the king's opponents from the palace and ran the League and foreign affairs on his own account, so that trust on either side was nil and any foreign enemy had an opening. The king then took the field himself, entered the Peloponnese twice, besieged Megalopolis and made the Macedonian army a permanent presence on the peninsula. Aratus was the real soul of the League but was chronically ill and never had troops of his own, so he could only hold things together through the League's machinery. On the Carthaginian side Hanno and Hannibal won Methone in a single night, and Hanno then operated around Euboea before being driven back in the naval action in the Thermaic Gulf; envoys from Pergamon and from Rhodes worked diplomatically to bring Macedon its allies. After the peace the regent Antigonus was recorded by the chronicler Polybius as having plotted to kill Philip V on his return to Macedon.
kits: 卡面上的斯巴達長矛，即希臘語所說的 dory，是這場戰爭裡最值得細看的兵器。它是兩米上下的一根直木槍，前端套一枚有中脊的葉形青銅矛頭，槍尾則留一段青銅套。那段銅套的用途不在裝飾：戰士可以把它插進地面，抵住自己的盾牌形成支撐；也可以把長矛斜舉在身前，用一整排的槍尾去頂住衝鋒的騎兵。方陣之所以能扛住衝撞，靠的就是這種前排互相支撐的結構，而 dory 正是這種結構的原型。戰爭期間，dory 仍配在兩種人手裡：一是希臘聯盟與埃托利亞、阿卡亞一系的重裝步兵；二是馬其頓軍中的希臘僱傭重裝步兵。腓力二世改革之後，薩里沙，也就是四至五米長的雙手長矛，已成為馬其頓方陣兵的制式兵器；腓力五世時代的標準大軍，是薩里沙方陣兵、持 dory 的僱傭重裝步兵、阿格里亞諾斯標槍手、弓箭手與騎兵組成的混合陣。因此卡面這件武器在戰役中的位置，是在方陣的側翼與外圍，替主力長矛方陣擋住散兵與騎兵的衝撞。同期埃托利亞人用纏皮條的短標槍，羅得島人與馬其頓海軍用三列槳戰艦與配重投石機，攻城一方備有撞錘與雲梯；羅馬方面雖未參戰，其縱隊兵種所配的標槍與橢圓盾，才是十年後決定希臘命運的東西。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card face, the Spartan dory, is the piece of equipment in this war most worth looking at closely. It is a straight wooden spear about two metres long, with a leaf-shaped bronze head with a central rib at the front and a short bronze socket at the butt. That socket is not decoration: a warrior could plant it in the ground and brace it against his own shield, or hold the spear angled forward so that a whole rank of butt-caps presented a wall against charging cavalry. The reason a phalanx could absorb an impact was precisely this structure of mutual support in the front rank, and the dory was its prototype. During the war the dory was still in the hands of two kinds of soldier: the hoplites of the Greek League and of the Aetolian and Achaean contingents, and the Greek mercenary hoplites in Macedon's own army. After the reforms of Philip II the sarissa, the two-handed spear of four or five metres, had become standard issue for Macedonian phalangites, and the standard army of Philip V's time was a mixed formation of sarissa phalangites, dory-armed mercenaries, Agrianian javelinmen, archers and cavalry. The position of the weapon on the card in this battle was therefore on the flank and in the outer ring, where it kept light troops and cavalry from crashing into the main body of long pikes. Alongside it the Aetolians used short javelins thrown with a leather thong, the Rhodians and the Macedonian navy worked with triremes and counterweight stone-throwers, and the besiegers brought rams and ladders; Rome, though it did not fight here, held the javelin and the oval shield of the manipular infantry that would decide Greece's fate ten years later.
tactics: 這場戰爭沒有單一決定性會戰，輸贏是在幾種不同的做法之間拉開的。安托古斯在底拉修斯之戰定下的部署是戰爭的基本形：方陣在平原上分左中右三段齊頭並進，兩翼騎兵搶先占據山脊，把對手拉下山來決戰；前排的方陣兵以盾與槍尾互相抵住，先用薩里沙的長程刺擊覆蓋前方空地，等敵人靠近才層層出槍，掩護後方的弓箭手與標槍手。腓力五世延用這套，並把方陣加深到十六排，讓前排出槍的長度伸到本排身後約兩米，敵人即使突破第一線，還要穿過五六層槍尖。埃托利亞人則完全不碰這一套：他們避免正面對撞，以輕兵不斷襲擾方陣的側翼與尾部，切糧道、燒田、圍困小城，逼馬其頓分兵，也讓對方無法安心圍城。迦太基的戰法在海上：突襲、登陸、夜襲據點，並在艦隊交鋒時用火攻與接舷。梅托涅的失守就是一場典型的夜襲，守軍不多，冬季陸軍不在，海軍從背海方向登陸，一夜之間奪下羅得島人的殖民地；埃雷特里亞與哈利斯也在同一套漏洞下被攻破。海上交鋒時，馬其頓的艦隊數量較少，但船身更大、划槳手更多，靠正面衝撞與接舷作戰；迦太基人企圖以載著燃燒物料的小艇順風推出，卻被反制，逐出塞薩利基灣。
tacticsEn: There is no single decisive engagement in this war; the result was settled by several different ways of fighting pulling against one another. The deployment Antigonus used at Sellasia is the basic shape of the whole campaign: the phalanx advanced in three divisions, left, centre and right, abreast on the plain, while cavalry on the flanks seized the ridges first and pulled the enemy down into a meeting on the ground; the front rank of the phalanx braced shield against butt and held, covering the empty space ahead with the long reach of the sarissas, and only closed in with successive thrusts as the enemy came on, sheltering the archers and javelinmen behind them. Philip V kept that system and deepened the phalanx to sixteen ranks, so that the spears of the leading files reached roughly two metres behind their own rank, and an enemy that broke the first line still had to cross five or six lines of points. The Aetolians refused to engage on those terms at all. They avoided collision in the open, harried the flanks and the rear of the phalanx, cut supply lines, burned the fields and blockaded small towns, forcing Macedon to divide its forces and preventing it from sitting down to a siege. Carthage's method was maritime: surprise, landing, night attacks on strongpoints, and in a fleet action the use of fire and boarding. The loss of Methone was a textbook night attack: the garrison was small, the land force was away in winter, a force landed on the seaward side and took the Rhodian colony in a single night; Eretria and Chalcis were broken in the same way. In the fighting at sea the Macedonian fleet was smaller, but its ships were larger and better crewed, and it worked by ramming and boarding; the Carthaginians tried to push out light boats loaded with burning material on the wind and were counterattacked, and driven out of the Thermaic Gulf.
data: 可核的數字不多，但幾個節點仍站得住。時間上，第一次馬其頓戰爭一般記為西元前215至205年，編年家波里比烏斯把它寫成一場對抗希臘聯盟的戰爭，發端在迦太基艦隊於愛琴海出現、梅托涅淪陷的那個作戰季。本戰爭可核的幾項數字：梅托涅失守在西元前214年冬，或215/214這個作戰季，城破只用一夜；依波里比烏斯記載，雅典派出二十五艘三列槳戰船，雖然遲到，未能救下梅托涅，仍協助安托古斯把迦太基艦隊逐出塞薩利基灣。先聲底拉修斯之戰（西元前222年）的編制由波里比烏斯留下：安托古斯投入步兵約兩萬，其中馬其頓方陣兵六千、僱傭重裝步兵六千（含克里特兵三千與麥加羅波利斯兵三千），輕兵約八千由他自領；騎兵共八千，其中馬其頓騎兵六千、伊利里亞騎兵二千，對手克里奧美尼只有騎兵三千、步兵六千。兵器尺度上，dory 長約兩米，槍尾青銅套數十公分；馬其頓薩里沙長約四至五米。腓力五世的十六排方陣，據波里比烏斯記載，前排出槍可達本排身後約兩米。停戰方面，西元前205年由羅馬使節蘇爾皮基烏斯·加利亞一行促成，和約主要是一筆分期償付的款項與彼此約束的安排；波里比烏斯並記錄馬其頓艦隊依令焚毀在科林斯的萊凱翁船塢，該艦隊在命令抵達前已自行焚毀，只餘一艘，駛出後也被點燃。整場戰爭歷時約十年。
dataEn: Few of the numbers can be checked, but several fixed points hold. In time, the First Macedonian War is generally dated from 215 to 205 BC, and the chronicler Polybius wrote it up as a war against the Hellenic League, beginning with the campaigning season in which the Carthaginian fleet appeared in the Aegean and Methone fell. On the figures: Methone was lost in the winter of 214 BC, or in the season of 215/214, and the town was taken in a single night; Polybius records that Athens sent twenty-five triremes, which arrived too late to save Methone but still helped Antigonus drive the Carthaginian fleet out of the Thermaic Gulf. For the antecedent, the order of battle at Sellasia in 222 BC is given by Polybius: Antigonus committed about twenty thousand foot, of whom six thousand were Macedonian phalangites and six thousand mercenary hoplites, including three thousand Cretans and three thousand Megalopolitans, with about eight thousand light troops under his own command; the cavalry numbered eight thousand in all, six thousand Macedonian and two thousand Illyrian, against Cleomenes's three thousand horsemen and six thousand foot. On dimensions, the dory ran to about two metres with a bronze butt socket of some tens of centimetres, and the Macedonian sarissa to four or five metres. Polybius describes Philip V's sixteen-rank phalanx as thrusting the spears of the leading files about two metres behind their own line. On the settlement: the peace was brokered in 205 BC by the Roman embassy of Publius Sulpicius Galba, and its main terms were a sum to be paid in instalments together with mutual obligations; Polybius also records that the Macedonian fleet was burned in the dockyard at Lechaeum in Corinth by order, the fleet having already destroyed itself before the order arrived, with a single ship left, launched and then fired as well. The war as a whole lasted about ten years.
cause: 打起來有四層原因。第一層是希臘本土的舊帳：同盟戰爭，也就是西元前220至217年的那場聯盟內戰之後，埃托利亞聯盟不肯接受科林斯同盟的霸權，安托古斯圍攻泰爾蒙不成，兩邊結下的仇記得很深。第二層是馬其頓的攝政糾紛：腓力五世九歲即位，阿拉圖斯掌聯盟與外交，國王一方掌軍，攝政軟禁了王宮中的反對者，把國王身邊的人換成自己的人，兩邊互信全無，等於給了任何外敵可乘之機。第三層是迦太基的戰略需要：坎尼之戰也就是西元前216年之後，迦太基無法從義大利抽身，便把戰火引向馬其頓的背後，用錢糧資助埃托利亞人，在愛琴海奪取據點，企圖把希臘變成義大利戰場的另一條戰線。腓力五世親政後兩度揮軍伯羅奔尼撒，圍困麥加羅波利斯，又插手斯巴達的形勢，這既把斯巴達推向埃托利亞一方，也讓本已脆弱的聯盟更難維持。於是本來只是聯盟內部的裂痕，變成一場有外力支持的全面戰爭。
causeEn: There were four layers of reason for the fighting. The first is an old account inside Greece: after the War of the Allies of 220 to 217 BC the Aetolian League would not accept the hegemony of the League of Corinth, Antigonus's siege of Thermon had failed, and the grievance was deep. The second is the regency struggle in Macedon: Philip V came to the throne at nine, Aratus held the League and foreign affairs while the king's own party held the army, the regent locked up the king's opponents inside the palace and filled the court with his own men, and with no trust on either side any foreign enemy had an opening. The third is Carthaginian strategy: after the battle of Cannae in 216 BC Carthage could not detach forces from Italy, so it carried the war to Macedon's rear, subsidised the Aetolians and seized bases in the Aegean, trying to make Greece the other front of the Italian war. Once Philip V took personal command he marched into the Peloponnese twice, besieged Megalopolis and interfered in Sparta's situation, which pushed Sparta towards the Aetolians and made an already fragile League harder to hold together. What had begun as an internal fracture inside the League thus became a general war with foreign support.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接結果，是希臘的自主能力又少了一分。最明顯的是聯盟內部的信任崩塌：阿卡亞聯盟對馬其頓的戒心，埃托利亞聯盟對科林斯同盟的敵意，兩者都往西邊去靠攏羅馬，羅馬的介入因此變得順理成章。戰爭消耗了埃托利亞與阿卡亞兩家的元氣，等到西元前200年羅馬正式對馬其頓宣戰、第二次馬其頓戰爭開打時，希臘人幾乎沒有能力作為獨立的第三方介入；辛諾菲利之戰（西元前197年）之後聯盟被解散，希臘城邦的自治幾乎走到盡頭。對馬其頓本身，腓力五世獲得的是實力與經驗：混合方陣的用法、常駐伯羅奔尼撒的財政開支，以及把希臘神廟的財物大批運回馬其頓的作風，希臘人對這批掠奪物的怨憤，成為日後他與羅馬交涉時最重的道德負債。對迦太基與羅馬而言，這場戰爭同樣關鍵：迦太基在希臘的支點被拔掉，馬其頓沒有餘力西進，羅馬得以在扎馬之戰（西元前202年）之後把西西里與地中海一併收入掌控。
impactEn: The direct effect of the war was to remove another measure of Greek independence. Most obvious is the collapse of trust inside the League: the Achaean League's suspicion of Macedon and the Aetolian League's hostility towards the League of Corinth both pushed westwards towards Rome, and Roman involvement followed logically. The war drained the Aetolians and the Achaeans of their strength, and by the time Rome declared war on Macedon in 200 BC and the Second Macedonian War opened, the Greeks had almost no capacity to act as an independent third party; after Cynoscephalae in 197 BC the League was dissolved, and the autonomy of the Greek city-states was very nearly finished. For Macedon itself, Philip V gained strength and experience: the working of the mixed phalanx, the cost of keeping an army permanently in the Peloponnese, and the habit of carrying great quantities of treasure from the Greek temples back to Macedon; the Greek resentment of that plunder became the heaviest moral liability he carried into his later dealings with Rome. For Carthage and Rome the war mattered just as much: the Carthaginian foothold in Greece was torn out, Macedon had no strength to advance west, and Rome was able, after Zama in 202 BC, to take Sicily and the Mediterranean into the same grasp.
result: 西元前205年，第一次馬其頓戰爭以一紙和約收場。波里比烏斯記載，羅馬使節蘇爾皮基烏斯·加利亞一行抵達希臘，與馬其頓攝政安托古斯、聯盟方面的阿拉圖斯談成一項和約：馬其頓付出代價，聯盟內部暫時安靜下來，戰爭至此終止。羅馬隨即下令焚毀停泊在科林斯萊凱翁船塢的馬其頓艦隊，該艦隊在命令抵達前已自行焚毀，只留一艘駛出後也被點燃，這一步既是羞辱，也是公開宣告：馬其頓不再是可以自立一方海上力量的對手。和約之後，腓力五世與攝政安托古斯撕破臉，後者曾策劃在國王歸國途中對他下手，被波里比烏斯記下，這道裂痕在幾年後的第二次馬其頓戰爭裡全面爆發。戰役本身沒有留下決定勝負的一役：梅托涅與埃維亞的失守、塞薩利基灣的海戰、伯羅奔尼撒的圍城，雙方都沒有全勝。真正的結果是聯盟瓦解、馬其頓的希臘政策轉向以軍力壓服，以及羅馬成為這片地中海唯一可以不經過許可就決定大事的力量。
resultEn: The First Macedonian War ended on a piece of paper in 205 BC. Polybius records that the Roman embassy of Publius Sulpicius Galba reached Greece and concluded a treaty with Antigonus the regent for Macedon and with Aratus for the League: Macedon paid a price, the League settled down for the time being, and the war was over. Rome then ordered the Macedonian fleet lying in the dockyard at Lechaeum in Corinth to be burned; the fleet had already destroyed itself before the order arrived, and only a single ship was left, launched and fired as well. The step was both a humiliation and a public declaration that Macedon was no longer a rival able to stand up as a naval power on its own. After the peace Philip V and the regent Antigonus fell out, and the regent was recorded by Polybius as having plotted to kill the king on his way home; that fissure broke out in full in the Second Macedonian War a few years later. No single engagement decided the campaign: the losses at Methone and Euboea, the naval action in the Thermaic Gulf and the sieges in the Peloponnese left both sides without a complete victory. The real results were the dissolution of the League, the turn of Macedonian policy in Greece towards ruling by force, and the fact that Rome had become the only power in this Mediterranean able to decide great matters without asking anyone's permission.
